answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require reputation to be carved in basalt, not written in sand: trust accumulates only through a long, public record of useful work. An umber shadow falls on accounts that appear overnight and claim deep expertise, since their history shows no spiral of gradual, peer-attested growth. Cheap identities can be minted by the thousand, but a slow, verifiable trail of real contributions cannot be faked at scale.
